title: Few words on screen
statement: Put few words on screen, the ones the voice is saying as it says them: in one study, two or three per slide helped retention.
detail:
The kit's standard: a plate shows only words the narration speaks while it is on screen
(`othello-unit-video/kit/docs/STANDARDS.md`). In one study, two or three printed words per slide improved retention
but not transfer (Mayer & Johnson 2008, https://doi.org/10.1037/0022-0663.100.2.380).
against:
for students with high
prior knowledge, added signals linking text and pictures were detrimental (Richter, Scheiter & Eitel 2018,
https://doi.org/10.1037/edu0000220).

evidence.quote: No decorative lists, invented text or unspoken recap on notebook pages
Audio is the MASTER CLOCK. Schedule every visual event off forced-alignment word timestamps. A reveal MUST NOT complete before its term is spoken.
≤1 NEW label per beat.
- The audio says *"Your three words are coming with us: That is the whole story, all five parts of the pattern."* It never says the words, which appear only on screen.
- The audio reads *"Your three words are coming with us: Next lesson the weasels strike…"*, so the three words are never spoken.
**Not covered:** the audio recordings themselves (only their text was compared with the screen text) and how the pages look in the renderer.
| **Word Length (Questions / Items)** | 5–10 words per question. | 10–15 words per question. | 15–25 words per question. |
The feedback should be between 1-4 complete sentences

remove redundant UI prose such as instructions whose action is already obvious
Ask appears in exactly one surface; Scout frames, never restates
- 25-word ceiling on any sentence a child must act on (story prose and taught frames exempt,
Long feedback text is itself a failure for Grade 3.
No on-screen text that merely duplicates speech
too much on screen
one attention target at a time; only the current sentence highlighted.
- You should avoid presenting redundant text that duplicates the speech.
- Karaoke subtitles (duplicating full narration text on screen)
The repeatable pattern is **one visible claim at a time, paced by voice**.
| Your words for this unit … | Iago at a window | the eight words appearing as spoken |
Never put every narrated word on screen at once.
| The organiser printed all eight words before they were spoken | the fourth piece is a picture of a page |
The cues follow speech, so two stills in scene 7 and 8 are held very briefly/late.
